faces.f: The clouds broke and the sun's rays burst forth; each foul beast in its turn faltered, and was gone.
D'Haren stared at the twisted lump of metal that had been a prized artifact. The fight was getting ugly.
Glory surged through her and radiance surrounded her. All things were possible with the blessing of the Divine.
Sometimes it's best to let sleeping dragons lie.
Any wall can be battered down, but at what cost?

"The day of spirits; my soul's calm retreat/ Which none disturb!"
—Henry Vaughan, "Silex Scintillans"
Theodar strode the battle lines, snatching swords with his bare hands and casting them aside until all cowered before him.
The elite guard of the Mesa High Priests, the Ivory Guardians, were created to protect the innocent and faithful. Some say their actions are above the law.
And then the Archangel Anthius spoke to them, saying, "Fear shall be vanquished by the Sword of Faith."

"Foolish wizard! As you tap the power of your lofty keep, so grows my strength."
—Malvern Xelionos, *Letters*
The purpose of any moat is to impede attack. Some are filled with water, some with thistles. Some are filled with things best left unseen.
A sign of battle, the Vultures circle and wait for the victorious to depart.
What walks on four legs in the morning, two legs in the afternoon, and three legs in the evening?
Few can withstand the wrath of the righteous.

"It was full of fire and smoke and light and . . . it drove between us and the Efrafans like a thousand thunderstorms with lightning."
—Richard Adams, *Watership Down*
I heard their eerie howling, the wolves calling their kindred across the frozen plains.

"Visions of glory, spare my aching sight,/ Ye unborn ages, crowd not on my soul!"
—Thomas Gray, *The Bard*
"Ow! Ow ow ow! Oooh, ow, OW!"
As many attackers were dazzled by the wall's beauty as were halted by its force.
The Azure Drake would be more powerful were it not so easily distracted.

"O! call back yesterday, bid time return."
—William Shakespeare, *King Richard the Second*

"Full fathom five thy father lies;/ Of his bones are coral made;/ Those are pearls that were his eyes;/ Nothing of him that doth fade,/ But doth suffer a sea-change/ Into something rich and strange." —William Shakespeare, *The Tempest*

"Adopt the character of the twisting octopus, which takes on the appearance of the nearby rock. Now follow in this direction, now turn a different hue."
—Theognis, *Elegies 1, 215*
Some people say that the world is round, and if you travel far enough you'll come to the other side, where everything is upside down.

"She grinned at me—a wicked grin. 'I hope you weren't relying too heavily on that, my dear.'"
—Medryn Silverwand, *Diary*
Many people say that no power can bring the mountains low. Many people are fools.

". . . [A]nd gives to airy nothing/ A local habitation and a name."
—William Shakespeare, *A Midsummer-Night's Dream*

". . . and the waters were a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left."
—Exodus, 14:22
Creatures of the Æther are notorious for neglecting their own well-being.
Nethya stiffened suddenly, head cocked as if straining to hear some distant sound, then fell lifeless to the ground.

"Leviathan, too! Can you catch him with a fish-hook/ or run a line round his tongue?"
—*Job 40:25*

"Walls of a castle are made out of stone,/ Walls of a house out of bricks or of wood./ My walls are made out of magic alone,/ Stronger than any that ever have stood."
—Chrysoberyl Earthsdaughter, *Incantations*
So confusing is the Wall's appearance that few of its victims even see it move.
Although greatly prized among falconers, the Zephyr Falcon is capricious and not easily tamed.
"'War is no picnic,' my father liked to say. But the Ants seemed to disagree." —*General Chanek Valteroth*
"Then flashed the living lightning from her eyes,/ And screams of horror rend th' affrighted skies." —Alexander Pope, *The Rape of the Lock*
The ritual of plucking out an eye to gain future sight is but a curse that enables the living to see their own deaths.
"If I must die, I will encounter darkness as a bride,/ And hug it in my arms." —William Shakespeare, *Measure for Measure*
"The highway of fear is the shortest route to defeat."
The voices of the dead ring in the heart long after they have faded from the ears.

"He knows he has a short span of life, that the day will come when he must pass through the wall of oblivion . . ."
—William Faulkner
"There is no calamity greater than lavish desires./ There is no greater guilt than discontentment./ And there is no greater disaster than greed." —*Tao Tê Ching 46*

". . . [T]he ghost rides forth to the scene of battle in nightly quest of his head . . . he sometimes passes along the Hollow, like a midnight blast . . ."
—Washington Irving, The Legend of Sleepy Hollow
The brightness of day turned in an instant to dusk as the swarm descended upon the battlefield.
You might leave here, Chenndra, should another take your place . . . .
"High on a throne of royal state . . . insatiate to pursue vain war with heav'n." —John Milton, *Paradise Lost*

"And a horror of outer darkness after,/ And dust returneth to dust again."
—Adam Lindsay Gordon, The Swimmer
"Today, for a lark, let's visit the plains. I'm sure we'll find something to entertain us."

She walks in the twilight, her steps make no sound,/ Her feet leave no tracks on the dew-covered ground./ Her hand gently beckons, she whispers your name—/ But those who go with her are never the same.
These days, some wizards are finding that they have a little too much spell left at the end of their mana.
Sometimes the smallest nuisance can be the greatest pain.
"'Tis now the very witching time of night,/ When churchyards yawn and hell itself breathes out/ Contagion to this world." —William Shakespeare, Hamlet

"Her lips suck forth; see, where it flies!"
—Christopher Marlowe, *The Tragical History of Doctor Faustus*
"An immense river of oblivion is sweeping us away into a nameless abyss." —Ernest Renan, *Souvenirs d'Enfance et de Jeunesse*

"Black spirits and white, red spirits and gray,/
Mingle, mingle, mingle, you that mingle may."
—Thomas Middleton, The Witch
"You know what I was,/ You see what I am: change me, change me!" —Randall
"In the drowsy dark cave of the mind dreams build their nest with fragments dropped from day's caravan." —Rabindranath Tagore
"For something is amiss or out of place/ When mice with wings can wear a human face." —Theodore Roethke, "The Bat"
The Walking Dead are the remains of freakish experiments by the Necromantic Lords.
Ærathi children who show promise are left to survive for a year in the wilderness. Those who return are shown the way of the Berserker.
Bogardan is a land as volatile as the creatures who live there.
"Kobolds are harmless." —Bearand the Bold, epitaph
Noted neither for their good looks nor their charm, Crimson Manticores can be fearsome allies. As dinner companions, however, they are best left alone.
The Crookshank military boasts a standing army of nearly twenty-four million, give or take twenty-two million.
Warriors of the Tsunami-nito School spend years in training to master the way of effortless effort.
"The bird of wonder dies, the maiden phoenix,/ Her ashes new-create another heir/ As great in admiration as herself." —William Shakespeare, *King Henry the Eighth*
The Frost Giants have been out in the cold a long, long time, but they have their rage to keep them warm.
"O! it is excellent/ To have a giant's strength, but it is tyrannous/ To use it like a giant." —William Shakespeare, *Measure for Measure*
On the morning of the Battle of Gal-Shan, the Sorcerer's cry rang out: "Let no bird fly, let no creature take wing, let all the battle join as one."

"The smith a mighty man is he/ With large and sinewy hands./ And the muscles of his brawny arms/ Are strong as iron bands."
—Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, The Village Blacksmith
"Joining this army is easy, boy. Just survive your first battle."
"One for all, all for one; we strike first, and then you're done!" —Oath of the Kobold Musketeers
The Taskmaster knows that there is no cure for the common Kobold.
Kher Keep is unique among fortresses: impervious to aerial assault but defenseless from the ground.
The Yeti's single greatest asset is its unnerving ability to blend in with its surroundings.
The thick, moving mass from the beginning of evolution swallows and digests the animate and inanimate as it unthinkingly strives to continue its existence.
"Hi! ni! ya! Behold the man of flint, that's me!/ Four lightnings zigzag from me, strike and return." —Navajo war chant

"O Great Captain, all is lost. They tunneled, they burrowed, they trenched. They sapped the strength of our defenses."
—Sorgus, *Chronicles of the Quarum Plains*

"Sometimes the bulls win, and sometimes the bears win. But the bulls have more fun."
—Anonymous
"Striking silent as a dream,/ Cutting short the strangled scream . . ." —Tobrian, "Watchdragon"
"Union may be strength, but it is mere blind brute strength unless wisely directed." —Samuel Butler
An ever-moving swarm of dust engulfs and disorients anything that comes near.
The ground shuddered violently and the earth seemed to come to life. The elemental force contained in the vast wall of earth was trapped, bent to its controller's will.
At a distance, we mistook the sound for a waterfall . . .
Like so many obstacles in life, the Wall of Opposition is but an illusion, held fast by the focus and belief of the one who creates it.
"'Tis the set of sails, and not the gales,/ Which tells us the way to go." —Ella Wheeler Wilcox
Unpredictable in the extreme, these carnivorous apes will prey even upon their own kind.
These stealthy felines have survived so many battles that some believe they must possess many lives.
Harthag gave a jolly laugh as he surveyed the army before him. "Ho ho ho! Midgets! You think you can stand in my way?"
"And the unclean spirits went out, and entered the swine; and the herd ran violently . . ." —Mark 5:13

"Sometimes it is better to be swift of foot than strong of swordarm."
—Elven Proverb
"Flittering, wheeling, / darting in to strike, and then / gone just as you blink." —"Dragonfly Haiku," poet unknown

"The turtle lives 'twixt plated decks/ Which practically conceal its sex./ I think it clever of the turtle/ In such a fix to be so fertile."
—Ogden Nash, "The Turtle"

"Then inch by inch out of the grass rose up the head and spread hood of Nag, the big black cobra, and he was five feet long from tongue to tail."
—Rudyard Kipling, *The Jungle Books*
The communal mind produces a savage strategy, yet no one could predict that this vicious crossbreed would unravel the secret of steel.
After the battle, an eerie silence gripped the forest. The losers' remains were lightly dusted with green.
"Many are in high place, and of renown: but mysteries are revealed unto the meek." —Ecclesiastes 3:19

"How dull it is to pause, to make an end,/ To rust unburnished, not to shine in use,/ As though to breathe were life!"
—Alfred, Lord Tennyson, "Ulysses"
Leave a bowl of milk on your doorstep each night for the brownies, or they'll cause you no end of mischief.
Fierce winds ripped across the tropical landscape. What they did not destroy with their fiery breath was washed away by torrential rain.
"Blow, winds, and crack your cheeks! rage! blow!" —William Shakespeare, *King Lear*
"Give them great meals of beef and iron and steel, they will eat like wolves and fight like devils." —William Shakespeare, *King Henry V*
". . . And at his passing, the bodies of the world's great warriors shall rise from their graves and follow him to battle." —*The Anvilonian Grimoire*
"Battles no longer served a purpose in Karakas." —Angus Mackenzie, *Diary*
He is devious and cunning, in both appearance and deed. Beware the Warbeard, for this brute bites as well as he barks!
Thundering down from Hammerheim, no foe could slow Bartel's charge.
"My power is as vast as the plains, my strength is that of mountains. Each wave that crashes upon the shore thunders like blood in my veins." —*Memoirs*
Urborg became the final resting place of many swordsmen of renown, their steel outmatched by the wiles of Gwendlyn.
Hail from Tolaria the ever changing 'Dane.
"You would never guess, at the terrifying sight of the man, that Hunding was as charming a companion as one could wish for."
Abandoning his sword to return to the lush forest of Pendelhaven, Jacques le Vert devoted his life to protecting the creatures of his homeland.
"Peace must prevail, even if the wicked must die."
Mightiest of the Cat Warriors, Jedit Ojanen forsook the forests of his tribe and took service with the Robaran Mercenaries, rising through their ranks to lead them in the battle for Efrava.
Once, the order of the Closed Fist reached throughout the Kb'Briann Highlands. Now, Jerrard alone remains to uphold their standard.
Popular indeed is the tale of how Kasimir was once a Holy man who renounced his order to take up the sword. But this tale is no more likely than any other.
"When milady was young, the sight of a rainbow would fill her soul with peace. As she grew, she learned to share her rapture with others." —*Lady Gabriella*

"I do not remember what he said to her. I remember her fiery eyes, fixed upon him for an instant. I remember a flash, and the hot breath of sudden flames made me turn away. When I looked again, Angus was gone." —A Wayfarer, on meeting Lady Orca
Livonya's own nature is a matter of mystery. Nothing is known for sure, merely rumors of unearthly stealth, and unholy alliances.
Marhault follows a strict philosophy, never letting emotions cloud his thoughts. No chance observer could imagine the rage in his heart.
We all know the legend: Pavel wanders the realms, helping those in greatest need. But is this a measure of his generosity, or of his obligation to atone?
"On the field of honor, a soldier need have no fear."
Ramirez DePietro is a most flamboyant pirate. Be careful not to believe his tall tales, especially when you ask his age.
"Political violence is a perfectly legitimate answer to the persecution handed down by dignitaries of the state."
"Remember Sir Shandlar! Remember and stand firm!" —rallying cry of the Eberyn militia
Even the brave have cause to tremble at the sight of Sivitri Scarzam. Who else has tamed Scarzam's Dragon?
Sunastian has roots in both sorcery and swordplay; he has learned never to depend too heavily on the latter.
Her given name has been lost in the mists of time. Legend says that her silent vigil will one day be ended by the one who, pure of heart and spirit, calls out that name again.
Administrator of the military state of Sheoltun, Tobias is the military right arm of the empire and the figurehead of its freedom.
"How can you accuse me of evil? Though these deeds be unsavory, no one will argue: good shall follow from them."
An explorer of the Æther, Tuknir often discovers himself in the most unusual physical realms.
A regular guest at the Royal Masquerade, Arien is the envy of the Court. She appears in a new costume every hour.
Al-abara simply laughed and lifted one finger, and the carpet carried her high out of our reach.
"A blast, an echo . . . then silence."
Nireya reached through the Gate, sensing the energies trapped beyond.
"'Tis distance lends enchantment to the view,/ And robes the mountain in its azure hue." —Thomas Campbell, "Pleasures of Hope"
"To make a prairie it takes a clover and one bee,/ One clover, and a bee,/ And revery." —Emily Dickinson
"This is the forest primeval. The murmuring pines and the hemlocks . . . / Stand like Druids of old." —Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, "Evangeline"
"Fairest Isle, all isles excelling,/ Seat of Pleasures, and of loves . . ." —John Dryden

"Resignedly beneath the sky/The melancholy waters lie./So blend the turrets and shadows there/That all seem pendulous in air,/While from a proud tower in town/Death looks gigantically down." —Edgar Allan Poe, "The City in the Sea"
"No rest. No mercy. No matter what."
Akroma asked for only one thing from her troops: unwavering, unconditional loyalty.
Redeemers rise with the sun, and the spirits of the people rise with them.
"We all borrowed life from the Ancestor to exist in this world. Today, I repay that debt."
"It's easy to lose sight of hope until you gaze out from my vantage point."
The slivers would survive, even at the expense of every other creature on Otaria.
"It is not yet time."

"I feed my hatred to the righteous and they join my crusade."
—Akroma, angelic avenger
"Every moment has its own savior."
Overcoming extinction has only made the slivers more determined to live.
The Mirari glows in her eyes.
His outer calm belies his inner fury.

"What cage would you rather be inside of than out?"
—Daru riddle
The first wave of slivers perished from the Riptide wizards' magic. The second wave shrugged off their spells like water.
"Now that I have your attention, perhaps I can tell you of the Order."
In the wretched depths of the Grand Coliseum, his soul shines like a single torch blazing in the night.

"Her voice is justice, clear and relentless."
—Akroma, angelic avenger
Their grieving faces tell far more than a list of casualties ever could.
Pathmages can open doors that aren't even there.
Some spies seek clarity. Others seek transparency.

"Her voice is insight, piercing and true."
—Ixidor, reality sculptor
Many wizards came to the Riptide Project hoping to return home with answers. Most, however, wouldn't return home at all.
The Mirari flares in his mind.
"I have no need of a map. The very continent itself guides my way."
"You cannot fight the storm."
To scrape out a living in Aphetto, wizards are reduced to selling rumors, lies, forgeries, or—if they get desperate enough—the truth.
Taking the form of a junior researcher, the first sliver slipped out of Riptide.
It may wear your face, but its mind is its own.
Though a completely artificial species, primocs are a natural fit for the skies of Otaria.
Those who lead others to wisdom become the wisest themselves.
It wants you to be its chum.
Once the last few slivers the Riptide Project controlled were dead, there was nothing to keep the island from being completely overrun.

"Species XR17 feeds upon the mental energies of its victims. This explains why the goblins remain unaffected."
—Riptide Project researcher
New insights yield new senses.

"Their blood is the nectar that nourishes the Cabal."
—Phage the Untouchable

"Death couldn't contain the slivers. What made us think we could?"
—Riptide Project researcher
Cabal clerics serve two masters: their patriarch and their god.
Death is a secret he is willing to share.
It strikes at your soul, heedless of your prayers.
It oozes death from every pore.
"A single dedicated mind can bring about the greatest destruction. That, or goblins—goblins work too."

"Goblins won't betray their own kind for any price. They'll do it for a very specific price."
—Phage the Untouchable

"Her voice is damnation, unyielding and certain."
—Phage the Untouchable
A cry of pain as it enters this world. A chorus of screams as it leaves.
Plague and death wrapped in one convenient package.
The Mirari festers in its flesh.
They pick at the remains of the city's corpse.

"Sure, I've seen agents of the Cabal here and there. Well, not here, and certainly not in any of the sliver labs. Oh dear, I've said too much."
—Apprentice researcher
It doesn't need to use its venom—it just needs you to know it can.
"The Cabal and the Order really aren't that different. After all, we are both empowered by faith."
Once it consecrated the dead. Now it desecrates them.
Measure its determination by the screams of its prey.
After breaking free from the Riptide Project, the slivers quickly adapted to life on Otaria—much to the dismay of life on Otaria.
The least popular goblins get the outer caves.

"Craghorns experience a wide range of emotions: rage, fury, anger . . ."
—Foothill guide
The Mirari burns in his heart.

"How do you stop a raptor from charging? No, seriously! Help!"
—Blarg, goblin jester
The more victims he kills, the more likely he is to get the right one.

"Did you know that wood burns even better than rocks?"
—Toggo, goblin weaponsmith
Most goblins leave behind a wake of destruction. A few goblins take one with them.
Giant-sized body. Goblin-sized brain.
Daru soldiers learned it's better to have a clean death from a sharp blade than to tangle with a goblin's rusted chains.
"Throw rocks at 'em! Throw spears at 'em! Throw Furt at 'em!"
Once they get the scent, there is no escape.

"Her voice is disaster, painful and final."
—Matoc, lavamancer
The goblins tracked the hystrodon with much stealth and cunning. Then they were eaten with much pain and yelling.
As malleable as molten steel, but as dangerous as the finished blade.

"The Skirk Ridge has many wonderful things to discover—like escape routes."
—Foothill guide
"I treat each day as your last."
"I order you to volunteer."
Once the goblins thought about it, they preferred being atop a slateback to being in front of, behind, or underneath one.

"The harder we press forward, the harder Krosa pushes us back."
—Aven scout
Lorians treat trees and prey the same way: by ripping them limb from limb.
Lucky victims get run over. Unlucky victims get run through.
Within weeks, more slivers nested in Otaria than ever existed on Rath.
"I lost one home when Yavimaya was destroyed. I will not lose another."
Mutated elves wondered if this was their final form, or if it was just another step.
Its diet consists of fruits, plants, small woodland animals, large woodland animals, woodlands, fruit groves, fruit farmers, and small cities.
A herd of one.

"New links are being added to the food chain on a daily basis."
—Riptide Project researcher
The first aven scout squad returned from Krosa with disturbing stories. The second returned with disturbing casualties.
The directors of the Riptide Project wanted instant results on the sliver experiments. They got their wish.

"It would take another apocalypse to stop the slivers now."
—Riptide Project researcher

"Her voice is wilderness, savage and pure."
—Kamahl, druid acolyte
The Mirari pulses in his veins.
Even through the Mirari's voice, the elves still hear the call of their kinship.
"Elves and beasts are tied together, and I am the knot that binds them."
As the Mirari's mutating effects grew out of control, centaurs and druids fled—but insects swarmed closer.
"Your words are meaningless. The rustling of leaves is the only language that makes any sense."
"Most insects have been drawn to the Mirari. But all that remain in Wirewood are under my care."

n: Huntmaster of the Fells // Ravager of the Fells

faces.f: Though giants are mortal, they live so long and on such a grand scale that many small folk don't believe they ever truly die.
Today it flies with the flock. Tomorrow it may wake to find them gone, its body in an unfamiliar form.

"Boom! Boom! Boots the size of oxcarts, then an axe like a falling sun. Elves scattered. Trees scattered. Even the hills ran for the hills!"
—*Clachan Tales*
Thanks to one champion archer, the true borders of Kinsbaile extend an arrow's flight beyond the buildings.
"We are a clachan of smiths. The forge is as comfortable to us as a small fire during a cool winter's evening."
His home clachan's familial spirit bolsters his own, but he will be ready to preside over the town as cenn only after he learns to project that strength to others.

"What does a mountain fear of a fly? Giants are barely aware of us, let alone afraid."
—Gaddock Teeg
"I've gotten close enough to a giant to smell his breath, but none has ever so much as spotted me. I wonder how long my record can extend?"

"It's a proven fact that sling-stones from the dawn side of the riverbank sail the farthest and truest."
—Deagan, cenn of Burrenton
The thoughtweft ties a clachan together. Sharing each other's hopes and fears, all the village's citizens spring into action upon the first threat to any one of them.
Made from whiskergill bones, merrow spinebows can fire bolts through tree trunks.
The giants believe the fossils they find in Lorwyn's rocky heights are dreams frozen in time, and they treasure them.
Though the currents of the Lanes shift every year, the merrow never lose track of where they are or where they are going.
Even when a giant's tantrum turns the sky into a chaotic gale, the path of the balloonist never falters.
"If a boggart even dares breathe near one of my kin, I'll know. And I'll not be happy."
Sometimes a curious giant singles out a "little one" to follow for a few days, never realizing the effect it will have on the little one's life.
Her ears are open to even the softest voice.
The empathetic nature of the thoughtweft allows kithkin healers to treat the cause of an illness rather than fight its symptoms.
"By tradition, we don't speak for two days after battle. If our deeds won't speak for themselves, what else could be said?"
A giant can brood over a grudge for decades, and woe to those who interrupt him.
If you pick a fight with one kithkin, be ready to fight them all.
Unaware of Lorwyn's diversity, it sees only itself, reflected a thousand times over.

"We merrows need not be disadvantaged when fighting on land. We lack the vulnerability of those who breathe only through their throats."
—Minnarin, merrow reejerey
A circle of sugar and a word of forbiddance.
The knights are a major attraction at every Lammastide festival. Teams of riders perform daring feats of flight to the delight of all below.
Changelings can alter shape based on what the beings around them desire most.

"When merrows talk, listeners grow fins."
—Kithkin saying
Kithkin weave together their very thoughts, creating a depth of cooperation unknown to other races.
In the backwaters of the Merrow Lanes lie stones scarred with tallies of countless generations, each representing a victory of merrow soldiers.
"You've discovered that boggarts bite, I see. And will the militia be chasing this lot? . . . Ah, you're staying in town to avoid Nath's hunt. Wise. Now this poultice . . ."
"Thoughtweft binds us together as one, part of an intricate pattern that would unravel if even one thread came loose."
There is nowhere on Lorwyn that the Merrow Lanes cannot go.

"My success at navigating the Dark Meanders irritates the Inkfathom school. They consider themselves peerless divers, but I try to remind them that they cannot own commodities like bravery and cunning."
Merrows consider themselves the keepers of Lorwyn's past—and consider it their duty to edit when necessary.
When all is taken away, all are equal.
Fallowsages debate whether the whiskergill is native to the Dark Meanders or merely dreamstuff made real.
The fae are so quick and their life spans so short that it's difficult to get retribution for their pranks.
Memories of ages past are said to swim the minds of lounging fallowsages.
Because of their capricious nature, faeries can serve as living lenses for disruptive magic.

"Petals within petals within petals, tadpole. The truth lurks below an opulence of illusion."
—Neerdiv, fallowsage
Victims spirited through a faerie ring find themselves stranded miles away.
The dreams of giants are as long as time and as deep as the earth. Thus they are prized by the dream-harvesting fae.

"None appreciate sun and shallows like those who have seen the depths."
—Lianda of the Stonybrook school
Schools meet and mingle on Lorwyn's riverways. In the bustling interplay, the merrow renew their sense of community as they sharpen their wits and hone their trading skills.
Steady and silent as the deep current, the reejerey guides the course of the school.
The fae know when they're not wanted. That's precisely why they show up.
"We see the same sky as you, just through a different lens."
Skilled merrow rudders ensure their charges arrive on time and without incident.
Some say the valley of Glen Elendra is mythical, and that rumors of its existence are nothing but a faerie prank. Others say it is the fae's most fiercely guarded secret.
One good mimic deserves another.
"I bring baubles of lore, lost secrets seined from the listening waves."
The Silvergill school monitors traffic on the Lanes, ensuring that the riffraff don't interfere with travelers.
One glamer leads him far from home. The next washes away his memory that home was ever anywhere but at her side.
"Water is in the air, the trees, and the earth. Understand its motion, speak its language, and the subtle currents that flow through all living things will fall under your command."

"We look in the river and see scattered stones. A merrow looks and sees a map of Lorwyn."
—Illulia, flamekin soulstoke
They ride on waves of Æther, washing out anything that might pollute the Merrow Lanes.
He paints with drop and shimmer a world that exists only in the wistful heart.
A changeling involuntarily mimics the nearest being at hand, sometimes trading a borrowed shell for borrowed claws.
Changeling magic grants unusual wishes.
Faeries hang beings that interest them as ornaments in the sky, each clique competing to outshine the prize of the last.
It absorbs the pain of other treefolk, which leaves it bitter, yet addicted to the sensation of agony.
Auntie excitedly held up the squalling newborn. "This one looks like Byoog! Maybe he'll tell us what he saw and felt in the beyond."
Auntie Flint lent axes to Nibb and Gyik, thinking they'd share their experiences with her. She's still waiting for them to come back.
At night, the faeries steal dreamstuff for their queen. At daybreak, countless creatures wake weak and hollow.
Among the boggarts, there is only one real rule: all new treasures and experiences must be shared. Those who hoard their gifts commit the one truly unforgivable sin.

"Those without beauty are Lorwyn's greatest tumor. The winnowers have an unpleasant duty, but a necessary one."
—Eidren, perfect of Lys Alana
Boggarts get so excited when they find something new to smash that they really don't notice who gets underfoot.
Beneath the fae's constant pranks runs a subtler undercurrent of mockery: the influence of Oona, their hidden queen.
One whiff of the sweet, pungent scent leads to euphoria—or to an early grave.
Leave it to a boggart to come up with a projectile as disgusting as it is deadly.
The scent of rot and vinegar fills the marsh, inviting boggarts from every warren to reunite and feast.
In desolate places, changelings may take the shape of fancies, or memories, or fears.

"And though she didn't get her honey, Auntie found something far more interesting."
—A tale of Auntie Grub
Snokk ran as fast as he could, but the sound of hooves grew ever louder in his ears.
Each bone honors its owner's best pranks.
In beauty-obsessed Lys Alana, one cut of her blade means the difference between a high society feast and raking through the dungheap for scraps.
One part cunning, one part wise, and many, many parts demented.

"This vulgar mimicry will end now."
—Desmera, perfect of Wren's Run
Winnowers live to eliminate eyeblights, creatures the elves deem too ugly to exist.
It hoards Lorwyn's rare sorrows.
Just as a changeling's influence can have dramatic effects, so too can its sudden withdrawal.
Smik learned the elvish dance quickly enough. The most difficult, yet most important step was to stay out of Nath's sight until called to perform.

"The unpredictable fae are just as likely to provide a blight as a boon."
—Desmera, perfect of Wren's Run

"Most faeries are harmless pranksters. Every now and again, though, you get one that crosses over from mischievous to malicious."
—Gaddock Teeg
Deep in Glen Elendra blossoms Oona, queen of the faeries, nourished by secrets and pollinated by stolen dreams.
Like being trapped in a perpetual sneeze, faerie-dust poisoning is both exhilarating and agonizing.
An elvish duel is a thing of beauty: the warriors' grace, the crash of steel, then the artful spray of blood.

"A good day in Goldmeadow is one in which I don't spend all evening picking quills out of my backside."
—Calydd, kithkin farmer
For disfigured elves, there are few choices beyond death or nettlevine.
Though they lack true flesh and bone of their own, changelings imitate either with equal ease.
Auntie Flint was the first to pioneer the spiderwig, a mass of arachnids intended to be worn rather than eaten.

"Why do our pies squeak? It's all the faeries, mice, and prickly-hogs we stuff inside."
—Borb of the Squeaking Pie warren
The crone's boughs creaked as she spoke. "You look peaked, little one. Come, sip from my warm brew. It'll have you blooming in no time."
"Any dream is a robust harvest. Still, I prefer the timeworn dreams, heavy with import, that haunt the obsessive mind."
"What do they need all this stuff for? They're dead. We're alive. Simple enough."
The angriest of giants are often the most skillful weaponsmiths. Their grudges fuel endless sessions at the forge, all the while growling ferociously to themselves.
"The changing kind suffers as we do. We must join as one to quench our tyrants!"
Among the solitude-loving giantkind, teamwork is unusual. But he appreciates hearing the occasional "Swing down and to your left."

"Reach in this hole, lose a hand. Reach in that hole, find a sparkly."
—Auntie wisdom
Boggarts revel in discovering new sensations, from the texture of an otter pellet to the squeak of a dying warren mate.

"Auntie pointed out to the faerie how much mischief a flying boggart could wreak, and a beautiful new friendship was born."
—A tale of Auntie Grub

"As far as I can tell, that frog dangling from the stick serves absolutely no purpose whatsoever."
—Gaddock Teeg
Flamekins' fires burn cool until they decide otherwise.

"The elves use treefolk to drive us away. It is time to remove their tools."
—Vessifrus, flamekin demagogue

Five-toed grave
—Kithkin phrase meaning "a giant's footprint"

"My ears say it hisses. My fingers say it burns."
—Auntie Wort

"The elves may try to confine us, but they will learn that our blazing spirit can never be suppressed."
—Vessifrus, flamekin demagogue
When he hits people, they stay hit.
Some flamekin warriors explore the art of coherence, an ancient discipline that harnesses the chaos of fire and focuses it with pinpoint precision.
The only feeling greater than hurling something a mile is crushing something else with it that was really, really irritating you.
Kith goats are just for practice. The real prize, of course, is a giant's cloudgoat.

"If you live on a giant's back, there's only one individual you'll ever need to fear."
—Gaddock Teeg
The flamekin are mere kindling for his warmth.

"Better to flare out than to gutter."
—Flamekin expression

"Things were popping like corn in a skillet. Olly landed in the pig pen with his prize sow on top of him, both squealin' like boggarts."
—Deagan, cenn of Burrenton
Elementals are ideas given form. This one is the idea of "smashitude."
A light an army can follow.
"I don't know why the little one was so mad. He said to put him down, and I put him down."
The oil sloshes against his skull as he nears his destination: the Frogtosser Games and the lighting of the Flaming Boggart.

"First it was plovers and mulldrifters. Now it's knitting needles the size of javelins."
—Calydd, kithkin farmer
"Be silent and listen to your inner fire. Only then can you walk the Path of Flame."
When provoked, a flamekin's inner fire burns far hotter than any giant's forge.
Boggarts constantly strive to outdo each other with the things they bring back to the warren, each hoping the exploit will become as well-known as those of Auntie Grub.
A hundred generations has he mentored, a hundred armies has he crushed beneath his feet, yet only a hundred words has he ever spoken, each more revered than a hundred books.

"Auntie Grub had caught a goat, a bleating doe that still squirmed in her arms. At the same time, her warren decided to share with her a sensory greeting of hot tar . . . ."
—A tale of Auntie Grub

"After Auntie brushed the soot from her eyes, she discovered something wonderful: the fire had turned the goat into something that smelled delicious."
—A tale of Auntie Grub
He cares not for the disasters his storm brings as long as his path ahead is clear.
"I knew that trick long before your great-grandmother's great-grandmother was born."
"If you want to test wisdom, offer it to fools and watch how they tear it up."

"Clever folk build their homes near cloudcrowns. If a hawk or even just a faerie tries to swoop in, it'll get swatted from here to Cloverdell."
—Calydd, kithkin farmer
"How do the vinebred feel? Fah! We do not ask the puppet how it feels when the puppeteer bids it dance."
"No matter how adept our artistic skill, our effigies can never hope to capture the vibrant beauty of a living elf. Perhaps that is truly why we mourn."
The hardest lesson for any elf to learn is humility. It takes a giant to teach that.
The faultless and immaculate castes form the lower tiers of elvish society, with the exquisite caste above them. At the pinnacle is the perfect, a consummate blend of aristocrat and predator.
From mite to mighty.

Calm as a wisent's watch
—Elvish expression meaning "safe"
Pretty, valuable, and delicious—a boggart thief's trifecta.
Desmera blinded her seers so that her beauty would be the last image burned in their memories. The act only deepened their insight.
Although they're protective of all creatures, many treefolk are especially fond of the empathic kithkin.
Elvish battle-magic has evolved two specialties: inflicting wounds that scar, and healing wounds without scarring. Politics determines the recipients of each.
"Springjacks and faeries can be difficult to hunt, but my favorite prey are the flamekin. They never fail to put up a worthy fight when cornered."
Elves of the immaculate class weave flora into living creatures—sometimes to endorse an elite warrior, sometimes to create a breathing work of art.
In a culture of beauty, the most beautiful are worshipped as gods.

"Tie a mouse under a bridge, and your cabbages will triple in size."
—Kithkin superstition
The kith dance their elaborate reels not merely to celebrate the events of their lives but to form an unbreakable bond of loyalty with their kin, a bond stronger than the fear of death itself.
Eidren's hunts are dangerous affairs. All dread the inevitable recounting of those who died while flushing out his prey.

"Which is more filled with poison: the flower of the moonglove or the minds of elves?"
—Vessifrus, flamekin demagogue
"A ribbon torn will ward away dark dreams."
Eidren, perfect of Lys Alana, ordered hundreds of trees uprooted and rearranged into a pattern he deemed beautiful. Thus the Gilt-Leaf Wood was born.
Bulgo paused, puzzled. What was that rustling sound, and why did he feel so stiff? And how could his *feet* be so thirsty?
From the highest tiers of Dawn's Light Palace to the deepest shade of Wren's Run, the silver notes of the horn shimmer through the air, and all who hear it feel its pull.
"Beauty determines value, and we determine beauty."
"Roam as you will, your roots remain in the strong earth of your Rising."

"All the sylvan secrets of this world are etched between my rings. The skinfolk's metal aberrations can rot between my roots."
—Colfenor, the Last Yew
"May you shade three generations of seedlings."
It takes a huntmaster's eye to discern the contours of mythical prey.
In his presence, an ordinary grove becomes a bastion to turn spells and break armies.

"If one can associate any virtue with the eyeblights, it is the talent some achieve in disposing of them. I have seen the slaying of boggarts raised nearly to an art form."
—Fiala, Gilt-Leaf winnower
Changelings cannot resist the draw of a new shape, even if doing so would be in their best interests.
"Each year that passes rings you inwardly with memory and might. Wield your heart, and the world will tremble."
So great is his wisdom and spirit that many who have met him say that they stood before a giant of a man and talked to the wisest of the four winds.
Even the oldest treefolk was but an acorn when Lorwyn's first mysteries were born.
A savage hunter with a prince's bearing.
"If there's a place worth going, the Merrow Lanes already do. And if there's a route worth taking, yours truly already has."
Auntie always knows which berries to lick, which kithkin to trick, and what to do when either goes wrong.
In a world of bright, cloudless skies, she is the dark storm on the horizon.
Lorwyn's stones resonate with the place from which they were hewed. Though taken far, still they call to their home when silence is upon the land.

"Apply orange leaf to a wound at dawn to clean it, at dusk to prevent the same injury from happening again."
—Kithkin superstition
Diluted, moonglove can etch living tissue. Concentrated, a drop will kill a giant.

"Without flame, there would be no iron tools, no cooked meals, no purge of old growth to make room for new."
—Brighthearth creed
When a changeling adopts a form no other changeling has taken, a rune appears in the caverns of Velis Vel to mark the event.
After trying mudskippers for an afternoon, Scratch decided that crickcarp made the best noise.
Mined from a cave in the Dark Meanders, it shines brightest when no one is looking.
Paradoxically, to tilt the massive jug for a sip, you'd need the energy of the giant's tonic.
It takes two to craft a mirror: a practiced metalsmith to silver one side and her own hazy reflection to polish the other.
For every tree who falls, there are countless sprouts waiting to rise.
The arbiter Galanda Feudkiller judges Lorwyn's squabbles from a lofty perspective.
The Stinkdrinker warren's hill of salvaged trinkets is large enough to cut a door in.
Dawn's Light, greatest palace of Gilt-Leaf Wood, is built on tiers of wood and power.
Protected by glamers and guile, Glen Elendra harbors the elusive Oona, queen of the fae.
Once each year, the sun's rays reach the hidden chamber of Velis Vel, and the changelings congregate from afar to bathe in the ever-shifting light.
Below the great river, a bustling hub channels the flow of merrow trade.
"In this place will I abide, and my heirs, unto the ending of the world."
Over all his works a dark smoke hung and wrapped itself about the sides of Orthanc.

"Beregond, if you can, do something to stop any dreadful thing from happening."
—Pippin
"The Realm of Sauron is ended forever!"
On the growing of vegetables, especially potatoes, Master Hamfast Gamgee was recognized as the leading authority by all in the neighborhood.
"Ónen i-Estel Edain, ú-chebin estel anim."

"I hope they haven't forgotten how to fight."
—Gimli

"This is worse than Mordor! Much worse, in a way. It comes home to you, as they say, because it is a home, and you remember it before it was all ruined."
—Sam
He hated the Ring and loved it, as he hated and loved himself.

"We must hasten. The beacons of Gondor are alight. War is kindled."
—Gandalf
"No Dwarf could be unmoved by such loveliness."
The Mûmakil of Harad were great beasts, like moving houses, capable of dragging huge towers and engines to war.

"Who can now hold the fords when the King of the Nine Riders comes?"
—Frodo

"Go! If you trouble us again, you will regret it."
—Merry

"Hope he rekindled, and in hope ended; over death, over dread, over doom lifted out of loss, out of life, unto long glory."
—*Eulogy to Théoden*

"The houses of the dead are no places for the living."
—Gandalf

"There we sat high up above the floods and watched the drowning of Isengard."
—Pippin

"What roads would any dare to tread if the Dúnedain were all gone into the grave?"
—Aragorn
"The world is full enough of hurts and mischances without wars to multiply them."
The one small garden of a free gardener was all Sam's need and due, not a garden swollen to a realm; his own hands to use, not the hands of others to command.
In a twinkling the table was laid. There was hot soup, cold meats, a blackberry tart, new loaves, slabs of butter, and half a ripe cheese: good plain food, as good as the Shire could show.

"Is it not a law in the City that those who wear the black and silver must stay in the Citadel?"
—Gandalf

"Go now, Wormtongue, whither you will. But then, if we ever meet again, I shall not be merciful."
—Théoden
Anything that Hobbits had no immediate use for, but were unwilling to throw away, they called a *mathom*. Their dwellings were apt to become rather crowded with mathoms.
"The enemy is at hand! We loosed every arrow that we had, and filled the Dike with Orcs. But it will not halt them long."
The Forest of Drúadan was granted to Ghân-buri-Ghân and his folk, to be their own forever.

"Last night I told you of Sauron, the Dark Lord. The rumors are true: he has arisen again."
—Gandalf

Three Rings for the Elven-kings under the sky,
Seven for the Dwarf-lords in their halls of stone,
Nine for Mortal Men doomed to die,
One for the Dark Lord on his dark throne
In the Land of Mordor where the Shadows lie.

"And in the night from Otherworld beyond the Sea there strong and free a storm arose . . ."
—*Song of Eärendil*

"A new Power is rising. Against it, the old allies and policies will not avail us at all. There is one choice before us."
—Saruman

"There are older and fouler things than Orcs in the deep places of the world."
—Gandalf
The Riders were overwhelmed: drowned in the roaring of the river as it carried them away.

"What aid have you ever brought, Stormcrow? And what aid do you bring now? It was aid from us that you sought the last time you were here."
—Wormtongue
Do not meddle in the affairs of Wizards, for they are subtle and quick to anger.

"The Great Ring shall go now to be an heirloom of the North Kingdom; but records of it shall be left in Gondor, lest a time come when the memory of these great matters shall grow dim."
—*Scroll of Isildur*
They looked east to the Shadow and west to the Twilight, and they plighted their troth and were glad.

"Smoke rises once more from Mount Doom. The power of the Black Land grows and we are hard beset."
—Boromir

"That is the business of Wizards: Wizards are always troubled about the future."
—Treebeard
Once or twice the travelers heard the rush and whine of swan-wings, and looking up they saw a great phalanx streaming along the sky.

Suddenly a song began: a cold murmur, rising and falling, grim, cold, heartless and miserable. The night was railing against the morning of which it was bereaved, and the cold was cursing the warmth for which it hungered.

"We have found many of our folk lying slain as they fled thither."
—Rider of Rohan
"Precious, precious, precious!"

It seemed to the tenders of the sick that on the Halfling and on the Lady of Rohan this malady lay heavily. Soon they began to fall down into the darkness, and as the sun turned west, a grey shadow crept over their faces.
They seemed like black holes in the deep shade behind them. Frodo thought that he heard a faint hiss as of venomous breath and felt a thin piercing chill.
"Curse the Isengarders! Uglúk u bagronk sha pushdug Saruman-glob búbhosh skai!"
Frodo was hardly less terrified than his companions; he was quaking as if he was bitter cold, but his terror was swallowed up in a sudden temptation to put on the Ring.

"But the Ringwraiths themselves cannot be so easily destroyed."
—Gandalf

"Regiments of black crows are flying all over. I do not know what they are about, but I think they are spying out the land."
—Gandalf

"They tried to pierce your heart with a Morgul-knife which remains in the wound. If they had succeeded, you would have become like they are, only weaker and under their command."
—Gandalf

Even Sam's vision in the Mirror had not prepared him. The Old Grange on the west side had been knocked down, and its place taken by rows of tarred sheds. All the chestnuts were gone. The banks and hedgerows were broken.
There are many evil and unfriendly things in the world that have little love for those who go on two legs.

"And there are some things, of course, whose side I am altogether *not* on: these *burárum*—these Orcs, and their masters."
—Treebeard

"This is the hour when we draw swords together!"
—Aragorn
"How long is it since Saruman bought you? What was the promised price?"
From far away, now dim, now growing, now mounting to the clouds, there came a drumming rumble, a roar, a long echoing roll of ruinous noise.

"Here, lord, is Herugrim, your ancient blade. It was found in Wormtongue's room. Many other things are there which men have missed."
—Háma, to Théoden
What could not a warrior do in this hour?

"But the Orcs have brought a devilry from Orthanc."
—Aragorn

"I have looked on Moria, and it is very great, but it has become dark and dreadful."
—Gimli

"A time may come soon when there will be need of valor without renown. Yet the deeds will not be less valiant because they are unpraised."
—Aragorn
The few survivors were rounded up in the woods, and those who surrendered were shown to the borders.

"I daresay there's more truth in some of them stories than you reckon."
—Sam
Of the seven Rings of Power the Dwarf-kings possessed, three Sauron has recovered, and the others the dragons have consumed.
Out from the beleaguered hills, knights of Gondor, Riders of Rohan, and Dúnedain of the North drove against their wavering foes, piercing the press with the thrust of bitter spears.
They began to throw missiles that passed right above the battlement and fell thudding within the first circle of the City.
A hundred ladders were raised against the battlements. Over the wall and under the wall the last assault came, sweeping like a dark wave upon a hill of sand.
To his dismay, he could not both fight and keep hold of his treasure.

Buckler and corslet, axe and sword,
And shining spears were laid in hoard.

"I thank you once more, and I bid you farewell. May your forest grow again in peace."
—Aragorn

"Radagast has much lore of herbs and beasts, and birds are especially his friends."
—Gandalf

"Radagast is, of course, a worthy Wizard, a master of shapes and changes of hue."
—Gandalf
The noise of bubbling waters came up from the foaming riverbed. Birds were singing, and a wholesome peace lay on the land.
Suddenly as they drew nearer, a terrific baying and barking broke out, and a loud voice was heard shouting: "Grip! Fang! Wolf! Come on, lads!"

"I sang of leaves, of leaves of gold, and leaves of gold there grew:
Of wind I sang, a wind there came and in
the branches blew."

"The Three Rings of the Elves were not made as weapons of war or conquest—that is not their power. Those who made them did not desire strength or domination or hoarded wealth, but understanding, making, and healing, to preserve all things unstained."
—Elrond

"In Dwimordene, in Lórien
Seldom have walked the feet of Men,
Few mortal eyes have seen the light
That lies there ever, long and bright.
Galadriel! Galadriel!"

"Do not think that only by singing amid the trees, nor even by the slender arrows of Elven- bows, is this land of Lothlórien maintained and defended against its Enemy."
—Galadriel

"Elves seldom give unguarded advice, for advice is a dangerous gift, even from the wise to the wise."
—Gildor

"The leaves were long, the grass was green,
The hemlock-umbels tall and fair,
And in the glade a light was seen
Of stars in shadow shimmering."
—*Tale of Tinúviel*

"It's a dangerous business, Frodo, going out of your door. You step into the Road, and if you don't keep your feet, there is no knowing where you might be swept off to."
—Bilbo
Ent the earthborn, old as mountains.

"Sing hey! for the bath at close of day
that washes the weary mud away!
A loon is he that will not sing:
O! Water Hot is a noble thing!"
—*The Bath Song*

"Do not let your hearts be troubled. Even now, there is hope left."
—Galadriel

"Huorns began to move south, as soon as the gates were shut again. Their business was with Orcs I think."
—Merry
They do not fear the Ringwraiths, for those who have dwelt in the Blessed Realm live at once in both worlds, and against both the Seen and the Unseen they have great power.

"There are no trees like the trees of that land.
For in the autumn their leaves fall not, but turn to gold."
—Legolas
All through the winter Sam remained as patient as he could. Spring surpassed his wildest hopes.

"I have seen three ages in the West of the world, and many defeats, and many fruitless victories."
—Elrond
Sam planted the little silver nut in the Party Field where the tree had once been, and he wondered what would come of it.
"Learn now the lore of Living Creatures!"
"*Lembas* is more strengthening than any food made by Men."

"Elves are wondrous fair to look upon, or so 'tis said."
—Faramir
There was a roar and a great confusion of noise. Fires leaped up and licked the roof. The throbbing grew to a great tumult, and the Mountain shook.

"The power of their master is in them, and they stand or fall by him."
—Gandalf
The swift growth of the wild with briar and eglantine and trailing clematis was already drawing a veil over this place.
